failures.answer: us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets expresses the capex metric only partially, and its figures cannot be read as one continuous comparable series with the metric's other concepts. Every observation filed under that concept carries mapping_fidelity PARTIAL and a registry mapping of mapping_type PARTIAL, with the note that it 'includes software and other intangible assets, which the property-and-equipment concept does not, so the series does not continue across the change.' The concept is a wider aggregate than the metric: its filed definition is the cash outflow for purchases of and capital improvements on property, plant and equipment, software, and other intangible assets, whereas capex as the registry defines it is cash outflow to acquire long-lived assets, on which sources differ as to whether software and intangibles are included. The mapping window is effective 2007-09-29 to 2014-09-27, with series_continues set to false and a recorded CONCEPT_MAPPING_BREAK of that kind over the same span; the break's explanation is recorded as NOT_EXPLAINED_BY_ST_EVA. The metric's other concept, us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, is mapped EXACT with series_continues true from 2013-09-28 onward, so the two concepts differ in scope. The overlap is where the two coexist: for FY2013 both report 8165000000 USD and for FY2014 both report 9571000000 USD, as do the overlapping quarters, but those are separate observations rather than a single joined series, and the period before 2013-09-28 has no property-and-equipment figures. The capex series as a whole is reported as comparable on the single us-gaap framework, 164 points, not truncated, with all 164 points SOURCE_REPORTED and UNVERIFIABLE because a single official source cannot cross-validate itself. That framework-level comparability does not license reading the two concepts' figures as one continuous comparable series: within the capex metric the ProductiveAssets segment stops at FY2014 and the property-and-equipment segment continues, and the registry records a mapping break between them.

screening_rows.answer: us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets expresses the capex metric only partially, and its figures cannot be read as one continuous comparable series with the metric's other concepts. Every observation filed under that concept carries mapping_fidelity PARTIAL and a registry mapping of mapping_type PARTIAL, with the note that it 'includes software and other intangible assets, which the property-and-equipment concept does not, so the series does not continue across the change.' The concept is a wider aggregate than the metric: its filed definition is the cash outflow for purchases of and capital improvements on property, plant and equipment, software, and other intangible assets, whereas capex as the registry defines it is cash outflow to acquire long-lived assets, on which sources differ as to whether software and intangibles are included. The mapping window is effective 2007-09-29 to 2014-09-27, with series_continues set to false and a recorded CONCEPT_MAPPING_BREAK of that kind over the same span; the break's explanation is recorded as NOT_EXPLAINED_BY_ST_EVA. The metric's other concept, us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, is mapped EXACT with series_continues true from 2013-09-28 onward, so the two concepts differ in scope. The overlap is where the two coexist: for FY2013 both report 8165000000 USD and for FY2014 both report 9571000000 USD, as do the overlapping quarters, but those are separate observations rather than a single joined series, and the period before 2013-09-28 has no property-and-equipment figures. The capex series as a whole is reported as comparable on the single us-gaap framework, 164 points, not truncated, with all 164 points SOURCE_REPORTED and UNVERIFIABLE because a single official source cannot cross-validate itself. That framework-level comparability does not license reading the two concepts' figures as one continuous comparable series: within the capex metric the ProductiveAssets segment stops at FY2014 and the property-and-equipment segment continues, and the registry records a mapping break between them.
